identity.title: The evolution of the internal structure of massive star-forming regions in the Milky Way as revealed by ALMA
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We analyze the structure of 15 protocluster forming regions in the Milky Way using their $1.3$ mm continuum emission maps from the ALMA-IMF large program.

targets.name: 15 ALMA-IMF protocluster clouds (e.g. W43-MM1, W43-MM2, W43-MM3, W51-E, W51-IRS2, G333.60, G012.80)

evidence.quote: The sample consists of $15$ massive star forming regions located a distances between $\approx 2$ kpc to $5.5$ kpc and that are in different evolutionary stages.

findings_qualitative.value: All spectra deviate from a single power law and show a bump; more evolved clouds have bumps at larger scales

evidence.quote: the peaks of the spectra are present at larger physical scales that those found in the less evolved, young regions

claims.hypothesis: Does the size of the densest region depend on evolutionary stage?
claims.experiment: Delta-variance of 15 ALMA-IMF 1.3 mm maps correlated with evolutionary indicators
claims.result: L_hub anti-correlates with flux ratio and correlates with free-free surface density
claims.finding: Larger clumps are more evolved; gravity regulates growth with ongoing accretion

evidence.quote: the size of the densest regions in protocluster forming clouds is a direct indicator of its evolutionary stage
